scope: Curated, high-signal primary papers, professional research, public standards and platform guidance. Not a systematic review or an exhaustive list of all research.
policy: Each record states what a source supports and what it cannot prove. External articles are linked, not redistributed.

sources.title: Fitts (1954): Information capacity of the motor system
sources.insight: Experiments link pointing time with movement amplitude and target tolerance. Use target size and reachability as hypotheses for controls.
sources.limitation: Original controlled motor tasks do not set one universal minimum pixel size; apply current WCAG/platform rules.

sources.title: Hyman (1953): Stimulus information and reaction time
sources.insight: Choice reaction time is affected by the amount of stimulus information; use it to question unnecessarily complex selections.
sources.limitation: It is not evidence that all products should offer fewer than a fixed number of choices.

sources.title: Sweller (1988): Cognitive load during problem solving
sources.insight: High task demands can interfere with learning; separate teaching from demanding action in complex onboarding.
sources.limitation: Learning science is not an A/B result for any specific mobile onboarding design.

sources.title: Amershi et al. (2019): Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction
sources.insight: Eighteen empirically evaluated guidelines address what AI can do, expectations, feedback, correction and trust.
sources.limitation: Guidelines are broad and were evaluated in specified research settings; validate real models and users.

sources.title: Mathur et al. (2019): Dark Patterns at Scale
sources.insight: A large web crawl cataloged deceptive commerce patterns; design rejection tests for fake urgency, hidden costs, pressured choices.
sources.limitation: Observational crawl of shopping websites, not a universal present-day prevalence estimate.

sources.title: Lewis et al. (2013): UMUX-LITE
sources.insight: A brief usefulness-and-usability questionnaire can complement observed task results.
sources.limitation: Self-reported usability does not replace direct observation or accessibility testing.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group: Recognition Rather Than Recall
sources.insight: Offer visible choices, labels and history instead of forcing users to recall hidden commands.
sources.limitation: A design heuristic, not causal evidence for a specific app.

sources.title: Nielsen Norman Group: 10 Usability Heuristics
sources.insight: System status, matching real-world language, control, consistency, error prevention and recovery guide reviews.
sources.limitation: Heuristic evaluations should be paired with user/task evidence.

sources.title: W3C: ARIA Authoring Practices patterns
sources.insight: Detailed interaction contracts for comboboxes, dialogs, menus, tabs, treegrids and more.
sources.limitation: ARIA examples require correct semantics, keyboard support and testing; native HTML is preferred when sufficient.

sources.title: W3C: Modal dialog pattern
sources.insight: Dialogs require contained focus, appropriately inert background and an exit route.
sources.limitation: Do not use dialogs for ordinary reading/navigation; exact focus choices depend on content.

sources.title: W3C: Cognitive Accessibility
sources.insight: Support comprehension, memory and attention with clear language, predictable structure and multiple cues.
sources.limitation: W3C cognitive guidance includes supplemental notes, not all are WCAG success criteria.

sources.title: W3C: Clear and Understandable Content
sources.insight: Use simple, direct language and recognizable chunks to improve comprehension.
sources.limitation: Supplemental guidance beyond minimum WCAG criteria, not a certification checklist.

sources.title: W3C: Handling bidirectional text in HTML
sources.insight: Use correct direction attributes for mixed RTL/LTR content and test data, controls and reading order.
sources.limitation: Directional handling varies by language and content; avoid automatically reversing everything.

sources.title: W3C: Animation from Interactions
sources.insight: Provide ways to disable nonessential motion triggered by interaction when required.
sources.limitation: Specific success criterion has applicability conditions; not a ban on all animation.

sources.title: W3C: Target Size (Minimum)
sources.insight: Target size and spacing have accessibility implications, especially for pointer users.
sources.limitation: Includes exceptions and nuanced counting; do not substitute this for native platform guidance.

sources.title: GOV.UK Design System: Patterns
sources.insight: Task-focused patterns for dates, accounts, checking answers, identity, forms and service recovery.
sources.limitation: UK public services are a specific domain; adapt patterns to local laws and audiences.

sources.title: GOV.UK: Error summary
sources.insight: For multi-field validation, summarize mistakes and link to fields while giving local repair instructions.
sources.limitation: This is GOV.UK's explicit implementation pattern, not mandatory for every web form.

sources.title: GOV.UK: Ask users for dates
sources.insight: Dates of birth, future bookings and approximate dates require different input approaches.
sources.limitation: This guidance is context-specific; test users, locale and format.

sources.title: GOV.UK: Complete multiple tasks
sources.insight: Group long processes into legible tasks with visible status and resumable progress.
sources.limitation: Only helps sufficiently complex workflows; a short flow does not need a task dashboard.

sources.title: U.S. Web Design System: Design Principles
sources.insight: Real user needs, accessibility, consistency and iteration should govern component selection.
sources.limitation: Government context; useful general principles but not product-specific experimental evidence.

sources.title: U.S. Web Design System: Form
sources.insight: Preserve DOM reading order and associate instructions/errors with the relevant controls.
sources.limitation: USWDS patterns may not be ideal for every product domain and require implementation testing.

sources.title: U.S. Web Design System: Validation deprecation note
sources.insight: USWDS itself found usability/accessibility issues and deprecated its live validation component; test flashy validation before shipping.
sources.limitation: A useful counterexample, not proof that all inline validation is bad.

sources.title: Baymard Institute: Ecommerce Search UX
sources.insight: Search field, autocomplete and result guidance affect how customers find items.
sources.limitation: Study context is ecommerce, and many detailed findings are proprietary.

sources.title: Baymard Institute: Product Lists & Filtering UX
sources.insight: Comparable result cards and meaningful filters support narrowing large commerce catalogs.
sources.limitation: Tests focus on ecommerce; do not infer a universal filter placement or sales uplift.

sources.title: Apple HIG: Tab bars (2026)
sources.insight: Use tab bars for top-level destinations, preserving navigation state across tabs.
sources.limitation: Do not repurpose tabs as action buttons; platform guidance can change.

sources.title: Apple HIG: Sheets (2026)
sources.insight: Use sheets for a scoped task related to the underlying view rather than permanent navigation.
sources.limitation: Different sheet behavior on iOS/iPadOS and other Apple platforms.

sources.title: Apple HIG: Layout
sources.insight: Group related information, respect safe areas and let essential content remain discoverable.
sources.limitation: Platform rules change and require testing across supported form factors.

sources.title: Apple HIG: Materials and Liquid Glass
sources.insight: Distinguish functional navigation/control materials from the underlying content surfaces.
sources.limitation: Materials differ by OS/version and are not an instruction to imitate system visuals everywhere.

sources.title: Android: Adaptive App Quality Guidelines
sources.insight: Design responsive flows across phones, tablets, foldables, desktop modes and relevant input types.
sources.limitation: The checklist is tiered; apply requirements appropriate to an app's supported form factors.

sources.title: Android: Core App Quality Guidelines
sources.insight: Support predictable navigation, platform behaviors, stable UI and permissions.
sources.limitation: Store acceptance and performance need actual device/release testing.

sources.title: Google PAIR: Human-centered AI Patterns
sources.insight: Determine whether AI helps, set expectations, explain boundaries, preserve feedback and reversibility.
sources.limitation: A practitioner framework informed by research, not a guarantee of model accuracy.

sources.title: Google: Trusted AI Product Guidebook Codelab
sources.insight: Apply concrete exercises to AI mental models, explanation and calibrated trust.
sources.limitation: Teaching exercise rather than direct evidence of conversion or safety.

sources.title: NIST: AI Risk Management Framework
sources.insight: Use governance, measurement and documented risks for consequential AI product features.
sources.limitation: Voluntary framework; does not replace applicable regulation or a security review.

sources.title: OWASP: 2025 LLM Top 10 Risks
sources.insight: Address prompt injection, sensitive information disclosure, supply chain and excessive agency in AI UX.
sources.limitation: A threat-modeling reference, not evidence that a specific integration is secure.

sources.title: MDN: View Transition API
sources.insight: Use transitions to maintain continuity across DOM/navigation state changes where browser support allows.
sources.limitation: Progressive enhancement, motion preferences and browser compatibility required.

sources.title: Google web.dev: Core Web Vitals
sources.insight: Measure loading, input responsiveness and visual stability with suitable tooling.
sources.limitation: Good Core Web Vitals do not alone guarantee accessibility, ranking or sales.

sources.title: W3C: WCAG 2.2
sources.insight: Reference keyboard, perceivability, focus, zoom and target-size conformance criteria.
sources.limitation: Automated tooling can only cover some requirements; human review required.

sources.title: Brooke (1996): System Usability Scale
sources.insight: A standard post-task perceived-usability scale can complement observed task completion.
sources.limitation: SUS measures subjective perception, not task efficiency or accessibility conformance.

sources.title: Apple HIG: Onboarding
sources.insight: Keep first-run teaching optional and rooted in action where it is necessary.
sources.limitation: Not a requirement that every app should have an onboarding flow.

sources.title: NN/g: Progressive Disclosure
sources.insight: Progressively reveal advanced functionality without hiding essential actions or context.
sources.limitation: Complexity management principle; test whether novices can still discover what they need.

sources.title: W3C WAI: Forms Tutorial
sources.insight: Ensure labels, instructions, grouping and error identification are available to assistive technology.
sources.limitation: Examples are foundations and must be adapted to the actual platform/data.

sources.title: Android Developers: Build Accessible Apps
sources.insight: Use content descriptions, focus order and TalkBack testing for real task flows.
sources.limitation: API details and supported behavior depend on Android versions/framework.

sources.title: Adobe: React Aria accessibility patterns
sources.insight: Accessible component primitives can reduce custom interaction defects when used correctly.
sources.limitation: Framework implementation is not certification; verify your content and app behavior.

sources.title: Google Material Design 3
sources.insight: Use tokens, adaptive navigation and conventional interaction behavior as appropriate.
sources.limitation: Visual style guidance should be adapted rather than pasted without product context.
